text.cover_risk: Cover crops use soil water. WSU trials saw winter wheat yield about 20% less after forage cover crops in a dry spring and no difference in a wet one, and a review of temperate drylands found an average 11% drop.

cover_water.note: Uses soil water the next crop may need.

cover_income.note: Seed, planting and termination costs, with no immediate cash return.

text.rotation_benefit: WSU reports wheat after peas or lentils can yield 10 to 20% more than in a wheat-fallow rotation, and pulses help with grass weeds and disease.
text.rotation_risk: Markets, equipment and disease history for the new crop are not in our data.

rotation_water_fallow.note: Any crop draws on water a fallow year leaves in the soil; WSU rates grain legumes as moderate users.

rotation_income_fallow.note: Adds a harvest in a year that had none.

rotation_income.note: Depends on prices and yields, which are not in our data.

rotation_water_fallow_other.note: Any crop draws on water a fallow year leaves in the soil.
